title: Variable structure in the PDS 70 disc and uncertainties in radio-interferometric image restoration
question: What is the impact of the JvM correction on restored radio-interferometric image uncertainties, and what do alternative non-parametric imaging and multi-epoch visibility alignment reveal about the circum-planetary disc PDS 70c and the inner disc of PDS 70?

what.value: Stellar mass of ~0.9 M_sun and distance of 113.4 pc for PDS 70

evidence.quote: For a ∼ 0.9 M_⊙ star (Keppler et al. 2019), and at a distance of 113.4 pc, material at a radius of 0''.04 (4.5 au) would rotate by 62 deg, or 95 deg at 0''.03 (3.4 au).

what.value: Dust mass estimates for the CPD

evidence.quote: Using the dust mass estimates from Benisty et al. (2021) and Portilla-Revelo et al. (2022), the Rosseland opacities from Casassus et al. (2019b), and for a flat surface density out to 1 au in radius

external_data.citation: Benisty et al. (2021); Portilla-Revelo et al. (2022)

evidence.quote: Using the dust mass estimates from Benisty et al. (2021) and Portilla-Revelo et al. (2022), the Rosseland opacities from Casassus et al. (2019b), and for a flat surface density out to 1 au in radius

recipe.goal: Extract continuum visibility data and perform independent self-calibration and non-parametric imaging
recipe.method: Extract continuum visibilities and combine all spectral windows as in Benisty et al. (2021). Perform iterative self-calibration using OOselfcal (wrapping CASA gaincal and applycal with uvmem image models), starting with phase-only loops halving the solution interval from scan length (~50s) until PSNR decreases, followed by one amplitude+phase loop.
key_parameters: Initial solution interval = scan length (about 50s), halved each iteration
Briggs weighting r = 2 for PSNR checks; elliptical mask enclosing the source

recipe.goal: Align multi-epoch visibility datasets in the uv-plane
recipe.method: Extract subsets with identical spectral domains in LSRK, grid each dataset to a common uv-grid in natural weights using pyralysis, and minimize chi^2_align over overlapping uv-radii (where azimuthally averaged weights are >1/10 peak) to fit for a spatial shift (delta x) and flux scale factor (alpha_R) relative to LB19 using VisAlign.
key_parameters: 2048 x 2048 grid with pixel sizes of 3 mas (SB16/LB19) and 4 mas (IB17/LB19); uv-range 0.17 to 0.47 Mlambda (SB16/LB19) and 0.17 to 0.71 Mlambda (IB17/LB19)
assumptions: The bulk of PDS 70 is not time-variable between epochs

recipe.goal: Perform joint multi-epoch imaging and image restoration
recipe.method: Concatenate aligned visibility datasets directly, apply CASA statwt to recompute visibility weights from dispersion, run OOselfcal for joint self-calibration and uvmem modeling, and restore images with various Briggs robustness parameters without applying the JvM correction.
key_parameters: Briggs robustness r = 2.0 (LB19), r = 1 (LB19+SB16, LB19+SB16+IB17, IB17), r = 0.3 (SB16+IB17)

recipe.goal: Analyze variability and Keplerian rotation of PDS 70c and the inner disc
recipe.method: Measure flux density and upper limits for PDS 70c across epochs. Test orbital smearing by de-projecting LB19+SB16, rotating by Keplerian motion over 1.75 yr, re-projecting and averaging. Test point-source sensitivity in SB16+IB17 by injecting four 126 uJy fake point sources into residual visibilities. Compare face-on deprojected views of the inner disc across epochs.
key_parameters: Time interval = 1.75 yr; fake point source flux = 126 uJy; disc inclination i = 130 deg, PA = 160.4 deg
assumptions: Stellar mass = 0.9 M_sun, distance = 113.4 pc; flat surface density out to 1 au radius for CPD optical depth estimate

evidence.loc: 3.2.1 Noise level in the LB19 image
evidence.quote: The noise level reported in Fig. 4a, of 16.4 µJy beam^-1, appears to match the expected instrumental sensitivity.

answer_key.quantity: Peak intensity of PDS 70c in LB19 (r=2.0)

evidence.quote: This is best seen in Fig. 4a, with point-like signal reaching 126 µJy beam^-1, or 8σ.
Since its flux in LB19 is (126 ± 16.4) µJy beam^-1, if we assign the upper limit flux density to PDS 70c in IB17, then it brightened by 42% ± 13% in the interval of ∼ 1.75 yr between IB17 and LB19.

answer_key.quantity: Detection significance of PDS 70c in LB19

evidence.quote: In the case of PDS 70, we recover the detection of PDS 70c from the July 2019 data, but only at 8σ.
This is best seen in Fig. 4a, with point-like signal reaching 126 µJy beam^-1, or 8σ.

answer_key.quantity: Specific intensity at PDS 70c position in SB16+IB17 (r=0.3)

evidence.quote: The noise level in Fig. 4e being 31.9 µJy beam^-1, and since the data are aligned in position and flux, a 126 µJy point source should have been picked up at 4σ. Instead, the intensity at the location of PDS 70c is −51 µJy beam^-1.

answer_key.quantity: 3-sigma upper limit on PDS 70c flux density in IB17

evidence.quote: The non-detection of PDS 70c in IB17 (Fig. 4d) places a 3σ upper limit on its flux density of 89 µJy.

answer_key.quantity: Variability (brightening) of PDS 70c between IB17 and LB19 (1.75 yr)

evidence.quote: However, its non-detection in Dec. 2017 suggests that PDS 70c is variable by at least 42% ± 13% over a 1.75 yr time-span, so similar to models of the Hα variability.
Since its flux in LB19 is (126 ± 16.4) µJy beam^-1, if we assign the upper limit flux density to PDS 70c in IB17, then it brightened by 42% ± 13% in the interval of ∼ 1.75 yr between IB17 and LB19.

answer_key.quantity: Inner disc peak (Clump 1) offset from ring center

evidence.quote: We also pick up fine structure in the inner disc, such that its peak is offset by ∼ 0''.04 from the disc centre.
Intriguingly, Clump 1 is offset from the ring center by ∼ 0''.03 to 0''.04, which is comparable to the natural-weights beam.

answer_key.quantity: Azimuthal rotation of Clump 1 between SB16+IB17 and SB16+LB19

evidence.quote: We find Clump 1 offset by ∼ 70 deg in azimuth relative to SB16+LB19, as expected for Keplerian rotation if the centre of mass coincides with the ring center.

score_reason: All three ALMA project codes are stated and public, all five custom analysis/imaging codes (uvmem, OOselfcal, VisAlign, pyralysis, MPolarMaps) are open-source with URLs provided, and key quantitative parameters (grid sizes, uv-ranges, Briggs robust values, alignment shifts, scale factors, and noise levels) are thoroughly documented. Minor deductions for deferring initial continuum extraction details to Benisty et al. (2021) and not stating the CASA version.
rediscovery_reason: Public archival ALMA data, complete open-source software stack provided via GitHub/GitLab links, well-specified algorithmic steps, and clear numeric answer keys (alignment shifts, scale factors, PSNR values, and PDS 70c flux density and SNR).
